nodes.name: Zürich
nodes.planText: Full hour and, for a large part, half hour
nodes.note: By far the largest node of the network.

nodes.name: Bern
nodes.planText: Full hour and, for a large part, half hour
nodes.note: Seven long-distance trains stand in the station together just after the hour (derived).

nodes.name: Basel
nodes.planText: Full hour and, for a large part, half hour
nodes.note: Trains to Germany and to Luzern leave at :16 and :43, outside the node.

nodes.name: Winterthur
nodes.planText: Full hour and, for a large part, half hour

nodes.name: Lausanne
nodes.note: The trains to Biel leave at :04 and :34, outside the node.

nodes.name: Biel
nodes.note: Neither Zürich nor Basel can be reached from Biel in under an hour.

nodes.name: Luzern
nodes.arr: from Bern at :01, Basel :05, Zürich :25 and :51
nodes.note: Planned at 15 and 45 on the strength of a 38-minute run from Zürich through two new tunnels, of which one was not built. In 2026 its trains gather around the hour and the half hour; the Gotthard trains leave at :18 and :54.

nodes.name: St. Gallen
nodes.note: Under an hour from Zürich was a target of the second stage (unverified).

nodes.name: Visp
nodes.note: Became a node when the Lötschberg base tunnel of 2007 brought it under an hour from Bern (unverified).

nodes.name: Interlaken Ost
nodes.note: Also built up as a node (unverified).

nodes.name: Genève
nodes.note: End of the line; 39 minutes from Lausanne.

nodes.name: Lugano
nodes.note: Just under two hours from Zürich since the Gotthard and Ceneri base tunnels.

edges.nowText: 56 minutes: leaves Zürich at :02, arrives at :58
edges.bought: The new line between Mattstetten and Rothrist. 58 minutes in December 2004, 56 since trains run at 200 km/h on it (unverified).

edges.nowText: 56 minutes: leaves Bern at :04, arrives at :00
edges.bought: The same new line, and the Adler tunnel of 2000 near Basel.

edges.nowText: 61 minutes: leaves Bern at :00, arrives at :01
edges.bought: The same new line. 60 minutes in 2004 (unverified).

edges.nowText: 52 to 54 minutes: leaves Zürich at :34, arrives at :26
44 minutes: leaves Zürich at :07, arrives at :51
edges.bought: The tunnel from Zürich to Thalwil of 2003. The second tunnel was not built.

edges.nowText: 58 to 60 minutes: leaves Zürich at :02, arrives at :02
edges.planText: under 60 minutes (target of the second stage)
edges.before: cut by about 18 minutes in December 2015
edges.bought: The cross-city line in Zürich, which ended the reversal there, with dropped stops and tilting trains.

edges.nowText: 25 minutes by Intercity from the through platforms
69 minutes: leaves Bern at :34, arrives at :43
edges.bought: Nothing yet: most of the new line was deferred in 1994, and the tilting technology that was to replace it was dropped in 2022. The concept for 2035 assumes 68 minutes.

edges.nowText: 68 minutes: leaves Lausanne at :34, arrives at :42
edges.bought: Tilting trains instead of a new line. The 2026 time is back to the time before.

edges.nowText: 71 minutes: leaves Biel at :45, arrives at :56
edges.bought: Tilting trains, and a link from the new line towards Solothurn.

edges.nowText: 57 minutes: leaves Bern at :07, arrives at :04
edges.bought: The Lötschberg base tunnel of 2007; 54 minutes when it opened.

edges.nowText: 54 to 55 minutes: leaves Bern at :04, arrives at :59
39 minutes: leaves Lausanne at :46, arrives at :25
74 minutes: leaves Zürich at :38, arrives at :52
1 h 53: leaves Zürich at :05, arrives at :58
edges.bought: The Gotthard base tunnel of 2016 and the Ceneri base tunnel of 2020.
